decisions.statement: Grow this capability through independently proven atomic scenario contracts (one obligation, one responsibility, one artifact) rather than one large upfront contract; this is the first slice, covering only the minimum-Node-version obligation.
The closed-world ontology runtime cannot parse semver strings, so the input contract uses a pre-derived availableMemoryMb integer rather than the full nodeVersion string intent.md illustrates.
Headroom ratios remain outside this admitted capability because the live projection left that policy unresolved.

deviations.impact: Callers must supply availableMemoryMb directly; full nodeVersion string display is deferred to a later slice.
deviations.implemented: Compare a pre-derived integer availableMemoryMb against a required-memory fact.
deviations.proposed: Compare full semver strings (e.g. "24.2.0" >= "24.0.0") as illustrated in docs/intent.md.
deviations.reason: The runtime's compare-bounded primitive requires both operands to be small (<=64 value domain) bounded integers; there is no string-parsing primitive.
